scenes.speaker: a
scenes.narration: Should we put the login service in front of every request? I say yes, because one missed check is a breach.

scenes.speaker: b
scenes.narration: Hold on. Every request means one more network hop, and our budget is two hundred milliseconds in total.

scenes.speaker: a
scenes.narration: Then check only at the edge. A signed token is verified in under a millisecond, so the hop to the service costs nothing.

scenes.speaker: b
scenes.narration: Tokens can outlive revoked accounts. That is the gap I worry about. How long do you let a stale token live?

scenes.speaker: a
scenes.narration: Five minutes, so every token is short-lived. A deny list at the edge handles revocation, and writes get a full check. Speed, with a short window.

scenes.speaker: b
scenes.narration: Fine, I accept that. Remember three things: verify at the edge, keep tokens short, and check writes in full.
